claim: GPApriori achieved up to 100x speedup on FIMI benchmarks using static bitsets.
quote: We tested our implementation with an Nvidia Tesla T10 graphic processor and demonstrate up to 100X speedup as compared with several state-of-the-art FIM algorithms on a CPU. In order to map the Apriori algorithm onto the SIMD execution model, we have designed a "static bitset" memory structure to represent the input database. [...] Our benchmark datasets are from the Frequent Itemset Mining Repository [10]
bib_notes: OK. Crossref/DBLP: Fan Zhang, Yan Zhang, Jason D. Bakos, "GPApriori: GPU-Accelerated Frequent Itemset Mining", 2011 IEEE Int. Conf. Cluster Computing, pp. 590-594, DOI 10.1109/CLUSTER.2011.61.
notes: "100X" appears only in the abstract and intro ("over 100x speed up"). The results section states smaller numbers: vs Borgelt Apriori "4X-10X speed up" on moderate datasets and "up ratio can reach up to 80X" on accidents; vs their own CPU code (CPU_TEST) "10X" on chess and "50X to 80X" on accidents; conclusion: "one to two order magnitude". Baselines are Apriori implementations only (Borgelt, Bodon, Goethals, CPU_TEST). GPU: one Tesla T10 of a Tesla S1070.

claim: Conventional approach that transfers full candidate sets and support arrays each iteration.
quote: In complete intersection, candidates are copied from main memory to graphic memory by host code, the GPU calculates their support ratio value by executing bitwise intersections on their vertical transaction lists, and the support value results are copied back to main memory.
grep: copied from main memory to graphic memory by host code
bib_notes: OK. Crossref/DBLP: Fan Zhang, Yan Zhang, Jason D. Bakos, "GPApriori: GPU-Accelerated Frequent Itemset Mining", 2011 IEEE Int. Conf. Cluster Computing, pp. 590-594, DOI 10.1109/CLUSTER.2011.61.
notes: Candidates are generated on the CPU (trie / equivalence-class join) and copied to the GPU per generation; support values copied back. Table 1: "GPApriori  Single thread GPU+ single thread CPU".

claim: Conventional GPU FIM implementations transfer transaction bitmaps, candidate sets and count arrays at each iteration (also line 402: "(1) they store the database as a dense bitmap that must be repeatedly transferred between CPU and GPU memory").
quote: Only the vertical lists of first generation will be saved in graphics memory, As shown in the example, the fourth generation is {(1,2,4,5), (1,2,4,6), (1,2,5,6),...}, and the supports are computed by intersecting (V1,V2,V4,V5), (V1,V2,V4,V6) and (V1,V2,V5,V6).
grep: Only the vertical lists of first generation will be
bib_notes: OK. Crossref/DBLP: Fan Zhang, Yan Zhang, Jason D. Bakos, "GPApriori: GPU-Accelerated Frequent Itemset Mining", 2011 IEEE Int. Conf. Cluster Computing, pp. 590-594, DOI 10.1109/CLUSTER.2011.61.
notes: Candidate sets and support results ARE transferred each generation (see line-194 entry), but the transaction bitsets (vertical lists of the first generation) stay resident in GPU memory and are not re-transferred; the paper motivates "complete intersection" precisely to avoid transferring intermediate candidate lists ("the cost of these additional logic operations is lower than performing the additional memory references required to transfer the candidates from the host"). So the "transaction bitmaps ... at each iteration" / "dense bitmap ... repeatedly transferred" part is contradicted for GPApriori.

quote: Experimental results show that GPApriori outperforms Borgelt Apriori on most of the moderate sized datasets with 4X-10X speed up and on a large dataset accident, the speed up ratio can reach up to 80X.
grep: 4X-10X speed up and on a large dataset accident
bib_notes: OK. Crossref/DBLP: Fan Zhang, Yan Zhang, Jason D. Bakos, "GPApriori: GPU-Accelerated Frequent Itemset Mining", 2011 IEEE Int. Conf. Cluster Computing, pp. 590-594, DOI 10.1109/CLUSTER.2011.61.
notes: Speedup figures in this source: 4X-10X (moderate datasets) and up to 80X (accidents) vs Borgelt Apriori; 10X (chess) and 50X-80X (accidents) vs CPU_TEST; "up to 100X" (abstract). No comparison with Eclat or FP-Growth ("Future work on the research includes how to parallelize other FIM algorithm such as FPGrowth and Eclat on GPU"). Largest dataset: accidents, 340,183 transactions (Table 2; also T40I10D100K 92,113; pumsb 49,046; chess 3196) - consistent with "at most a few million".
